# Sign in through an OIDC issuer

## Use when

Several apps should share one set of accounts: people sign in once at an
accounts hub (see `auth/accounts-hub`) or at an organisation's OpenID Connect
issuer, and every app signs them in from there. The app keeps its own `users`
rows and its own session; the issuer only proves who the person is.

## Do not use when

The app needs its own passwords (use `auth-provider-local-core`), or the product
has deliberately chosen Supabase (`auth/supabase-auth`). Install exactly one
`auth.service` provider.

## Product decisions

- Which issuer. A hub gives each app a registration token; other issuers
  (Google Workspace, Okta) give a fixed client id and secret instead.
- The button label people see.
- The production address, and who approves the app in the hub.
- Whether existing local accounts move to the hub (one-time commands below) or
  the app starts fresh.

## Invariants

- One client per app address. With a registration token the app registers
  itself the first time it is used from a new address (or at start when
  `APP_PUBLIC_URL` is set) and stores the client in `auth_oidc_clients`.
- The redirect URI is auth-web's login route, `AUTH_OIDC_REDIRECT_PATH`
  (`/auth/login`). Where to go afterwards travels in a sealed, ten-minute,
  single-use attempt cookie, never in the redirect URI.
- Every sign-in uses PKCE, `state`, `nonce` and the RFC 9207 `iss` check; ID
  tokens must name this issuer and this client.
- The app session is the app's own cookie (30 days), backed by
  `auth_oidc_sessions`. Signing out of the app does not sign out of the issuer
  unless the person asks for it.
- Secrets stay in Env, never in source.

## Framework APIs

- `@jskit-ai/auth-provider-oidc-core` provides `auth.service`, its migration and
  the `jskit-oidc-sign-in` command.
- `@jskit-ai/auth-provider-oidc-core/shared` exports `AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDER_ID`,
  `AUTH_OIDC_REDIRECT_PATH`, `AUTH_OIDC_LOGOUT_PATH` and
  `AUTH_OIDC_BACKCHANNEL_LOGOUT_PATH`.
- auth-web's login page shows the one button. Inside a frame (an editor
  Preview) it opens the issuer in a pop-up window and reloads signed in.

## Example files

`example/package.json` declares the provider and the login surface.
`example/.env.example` names every Env value without credentials.

## Variation points

- Static client (`AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`/`AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`) instead of
  the registration token; never both.
- `AUTH_OIDC_LABEL` for the button.
- A sign-out-everywhere link: `/api/auth/oidc/logout?everywhere=1` also ends the
  issuer session through its end-session endpoint.

## Verification

- Missing `AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER` shows "Sign-in is not set up yet" instead of a
  crash.
- Sign in unframed and inside the Preview frame; refresh stays signed in.
- A production address the hub has not approved yet reaches the hub's waiting
  page; a blocked one reads "Your accounts hub has blocked this app's address."
- Disabling the account in the hub ends the app session (back-channel logout).
- Preview identity (`tools/preview-identity`) still signs in as an existing
  `users` row.

## Avoid

- keeping the local provider installed alongside this one
- putting the return path or any secret in the redirect URI
- sharing one registered client between addresses
- running the account move commands without the person's explicit yes
